rationale: Shep asked for tomorrow's Saturday session to go straight to 20min threshold + 20min HM pace instead of the planned 20+10, worried the 10min block will feel too easy. The readiness evidence backs pushing further than planned: this is the best-recovered stretch of the block (HRV baseline 38.6->41.3 this week, RHR steady ~47.6-47.9, sleep scores 83-91), achilles has read 0 every day since mid-July bar two isolated 1s, no breathing complaints, and Wednesday's interval session was run comfortably (RPE 6, 'could have done more'). Moderate heat forecast for both Sat and Sun (20-22C) removes that as a constraint. But going straight to 20+20 does two things at once: it hands him, three weeks early and in one jump, the exact total quality volume (40min) currently scheduled as the 5 Sep key session, and it does it on the very first exposure to continuous HM-pace running this block - a stimulus his own achilles history says deserves gradual introduction, since intensity discipline (not mileage) was what caused the original injury. Compromise: move tomorrow to 20T+15H (what was already sitting on 29 Aug), and step 29 Aug up to 20T+20H. That gives him a real increase now, keeps the block progressing one step at a time toward the 5 Sep session (which removes the threshold buffer entirely and stays the qualitatively biggest step), and avoids stacking a first-time 20min goal-pace block onto an already-hard 20min threshold effort without a prior tolerance check.
